I'm going to get some downvotes, but here is my opinion/outlook: 

Long and short of it: law enforcement is present due to a suspect brandishing a firearm in public. The group of three matches the description, and suddenly, one individual refuses commands while his companions freeze in their tracks. The suspect walks off, still ignoring loud direct commands, then turns, sees the officers with weapons drawn still yelling commands, and does what any normal law-abiding citizen would do: he puts his hands on his head and gets on the ground. 

Oh, wait. He didn't. He proceeded to turn around and walk away from them backwards. They have drawn on him and are yelling commands... So he thinks to himself, "How about I just make direct eye contact and keep fiddling with my waistband."

Those officers are responding to a potentially hostile situation: someone brazen enough to wave a gun around in broad daylight, and of the individuals that match the description, two comply immediately while the primary target possible-suspect continues to ignore commands and engage in very risky behavior. These are the situations that make me not want to pursue a career in law enforcement: if I ended up getting killed by the perpetrator (and on video, no less), nearly everyone on this site would have been in an uproar about how I should have acted first.

There are a couple of people on here that I have to just say: you can't have it both ways. That's a difficult situation, and I don't think I would have reacted differently. There's a good chance, in that situation, I might have faced serious consequences if the suspect had a gun and decided to pull and fire with any hesitation on my part. Again, unfortunate circumstances. Sad all the way around.

I play a popular multiplayer game that features crossplay between consoles and PCs. It truly allows players from both platforms to compete together. This is likely the only type of cross-platform play that can be effectively implemented, as consoles do not typically compete with PC player numbers. It poses less risk for console developers to enable crossplay with PCs.

There’s no need for players to enter codes or choose specific player pools; everyone is mixed together in matches, with both console and PC players participating.

This capability exists and should be utilized, but financial considerations dominate the decision-making process. Companies will only pursue it if they see it as a sustainable revenue source, rather than as a gesture for the community or gaming enthusiasts.

This is a stark reality that many overlook. If all desired games supported crossplay, the only factor that would then matter is hardware specifications. Console manufacturers are reluctant to frequently release new hardware, as it represents a financial loss rather than a gain.
